   246	## 4. New exact fourth-moment expansion of the clipped initial energy

   248	Let h be any bounded even real zero-mean translation kernel on a compact
   249	abelian group equipped with Haar probability. For iid Haar \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_N\), set
   250	\[
   251	 H^h=N^{-1}\sum_{i<j}h(Y_i-Y_j),\quad
   252	 \mu_2=\int h^2,\quad \mu_4=\int h^4,\quad
   253	 \tau_h=\int h(z)^2(h*h)(z)dz,\quad
   254	 \chi_h=\int(h*h)(z)^2dz. \tag{4.1}
   255	\]
   256	Then the exact equality is
   257	\[
   258	\begin{split}
   259	 N^4\mathbb E(H^h)^4={}&{N\choose2}\mu_4
   260	   +18{N\choose3}\mu_2^2+36{N\choose3}\tau_h\\
   261	   &+18{N\choose4}\mu_2^2+72{N\choose4}\chi_h. \tag{4.2}
   262	\end{split}
   263	\]
   264	Binomial coefficients are zero if there are too few labels.

   266	Expand the fourth power into ordered quadruples of unordered edges. A
   267	vertex of degree one makes its term zero after integration in that
   268	coordinate, by the zero row. Thus at most four vertices survive. With
   269	two vertices all four edges agree. With three vertices, the surviving
   270	patterns are two doubled edges (three choices of center, six orders)
   271	or a triangle with one edge doubled (three choices, twelve orders).
   272	Their integrals are respectively \(\mu_2^2\) and \(\tau_h\). With four
   273	vertices, the patterns are two disjoint doubled edges (three matchings,
   274	six orders) or a four-cycle (three cycles, twenty-four orders), giving
   275	\(\mu_2^2\) and \(\chi_h\). This exhausts the degree count and proves
   276	all coefficients, including the two distinct occurrences of 18.

   279	\(|\tau_h|\le\mu_2^2\), \(0\le\chi_h\le\mu_2^2\). Consequently

   281	             \mathbb E(H^h)^4\le C(\mu_4/N^2+\mu_2^2). \tag{4.3}

The assertion is that the frozen Round 001 model admits the exact one-body
identity (2.3), the exact pair identities (3.6)--(3.7), and the martingale

permitted instance violating at least one of these equalities. The proof below

for it.

All measures are on \(\mathbb T^d=\mathbb R^d/\mathbb Z^d\), of Haar mass one.
Set \(\nu=\beta_N^{-1}\). The deterministic functions \(g,V\) are smooth and
periodic; \(g\) is real, even, and of zero mean. Write

\[
K=-\nabla g,\qquad b=-\nabla V,\qquad
u_t=b+K*\mu_t,\qquad L_t^0 f=u_t\cdot\nabla f+\nu\Delta f.
\tag{1.1}
\]

In particular \(K\) is odd and \(K(0)=0\). The deterministic probability density
\(\mu\) is smooth in space and sufficiently differentiable in time on the fixed
horizon \([0,T]\), and solves \(\partial_t\mu=(L_t^0)^*\mu\). The dossier assumes
strict positivity; the algebra itself uses only smoothness and probability mass.
The SDE is

\[
dx_i=\left(b(x_i)+\frac1N\sum_{j\ne i}K(x_i-x_j)\right)dt
       +\sqrt{2\nu}\,dW_i,
\qquad
\eta=\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\delta_{x_i},\quad \rho=\eta-\mu.
\tag{1.2}
\]

The Brownian motions are independent, and \(x_i\) are adapted solutions on the
usual filtered probability space. The initial law may be arbitrary; no
exchangeability or preparation assumption enters the identities. Smooth
bounded coefficients give the global SDE by Picard iteration; for fixed
Brownian paths the drift is globally Lipschitz on the compact configuration
space. All the martingales below are square integrable because their integrands

\[
\begin{split}
D_2[\Phi]&=\frac1{N^2}\sum_{i\ne j}\Phi(x_i,x_j),\\

P[\Phi]&=\frac12U_2[\Phi].
\end{split}
\tag{1.3}
\]

\[
